passages.context: The sudarin signal, read in the retrieved response for the whole mishnah, with the public-domain Torat Emet Hebrew of the same mishnah read alongside it. Registered as a positive control on the negative search reported by consuming publications: the rabbinic corpus does record a sudar used as a deliberate signal, and its sense is judicial, not domestic.
passages.notes: The word rendered scarf is ha-sudarin, the same word Greek borrowed as soudarion and Latin as sudarium. The Hebrew of the clause reads, in transliteration, ehad omed al petah beth din veha-sudarin beyado, and hallaz meniph ba-sudarin veha-sus rats u-ma'amido. The bracketed supplement is the translator's.

work.author: Rabbinic sages (tannaitic redaction)
work.description: The Mishnah's tractate on courts and capital procedure. At 6:1 it describes the procession to a stoning and the arrangement by which an argument for acquittal could still be heard: a man stands at the court door with the sudarin in his hand and waves it, and a horseman posted within sight rides to halt the execution. This is the one attested ancient Jewish use of a sudar as a deliberate signal. A locus is chapter.mishnah.
work.title: Mishnah Sanhedrin
